legal_units.title: Deduction of head office expenditure in case of non-residents.
legal_units.text: Irrespective of anything to the contrary contained in sections 26 to 54, in the case of a non-resident assessee, deduction of head office expenditure incurred by such assessee as is attributable to his business or profession in India, shall be allowed in computing the income chargeable under the head "Profits and gains of business or profession" subject to provisions of sub-section (2).
legal_units.retrieval_text: Section 60 Deduction of head office expenditure in case of non-residents. Section 60(1): Irrespective of anything to the contrary contained in sections 26 to 54, in the case of a non-resident assessee, deduction of head office expenditure incurred by such assessee as is attributable to his business or profession in India, shall be allowed in computing the income chargeable under the head "Profits and gains of business or profession" subject to provisions of sub-section (2).

legal_units.title: Deduction of head office expenditure in case of non-residents.
legal_units.text: The deduction allowable under sub-section (1) shall be restricted—
legal_units.retrieval_text: Section 60 Deduction of head office expenditure in case of non-residents. Section 60(2): The deduction allowable under sub-section (1) shall be restricted—

legal_units.text: if the adjusted total income of the assessee is a loss, to an upper monetary limit of 5% of the average adjusted total income of the assessee; or
legal_units.retrieval_text: Section 60 Deduction of head office expenditure in case of non-residents. Section 60(2): The deduction allowable under sub-section (1) shall be restricted— Section 60(2)(a): if the adjusted total income of the assessee is a loss, to an upper monetary limit of 5% of the average adjusted total income of the assessee; or

legal_units.title: Deduction of head office expenditure in case of non-residents.
legal_units.text: in any other case, to an upper monetary limit of 5% of the adjusted total income of the assessee.

Section 60(2): The deduction allowable under sub-section (1) shall be restricted— Section 60(2)(b): in any other case, to an upper monetary limit of 5% of the adjusted total income of the assessee.
